Well, from an evolutionary game theory perspective. As gametes are not made equal, female gametes generally are larger and more scarce, require more energy to produce. Also the mother who I would assume is generally female/the one usually bearing the child, this is a large commitment of resources and time.

Therefore its in the females best interest to properly vet the males, so that their finite gametes and time spent bearing the child is not wasted on an 'inferior' male (subjective of course) or in some species, on a male that will simply abscond and not support the mother/child.

Males on the other hand produce gametes at a much, much larger rate than females and after fertilization, basically do not need any more input and their genes have spread. Although it may be in the males best interest to also stick around and be picky, but not all species behave the same. If the male is generally having multiple offspring each year, it might be in its best interest (in terms of fitness) to just try and impregnate as many females as it can, and at least some of them will survive.

Sorry but this is incredibly lame, its simply mathematically impossible in this day and age.

I guess if you had a large, private island. Got a good initial population of a few thousand. Selectively interbred the fittest and strongest for a few millenia, then you might start getting somewhere. Maybe have a vetting process to get to your country, so only people matching your criteria will be allowed to enter from the outside world.

You'd probably need to have strict laws on reproduction to prevent any one else breeding, but putting all your resources and effort into this social engineering project, would leave you at the mercy of the other humans with actual countries and armies behind them.

So unfortunately, I just can't see it happening.
Yes, not all plants of one species are clones of eachother. Even then random mutation over successive generations, makes identical DNA in a species rather unlikely.

Almost all historic data shows that we are getting taller on average as a species, but this is more to do with nutrition.

Races are not really a biologically sound concept anyways, there will still be variation. Ethnic groups are also mainly social and cultural, and I feel we will not just decide to live in a single mono-culture.

I actually thought this a few years ago when I was younger, probabilistically it takes around 7 generations for there to be an ancestor who did not pass on any genes to you.

However because of crossing over, the previous assumption is blown out of the water. I think it'd be impossible to calculate with our current knowledge of genetics.

I'd also never been to this surgery before this week, why did they not tell me their procedure?
I mean I guess so, that is possible.

Why am I a snowflake when I literally never have any issue with the people I work with, just because you interact with uncouth people doesn't mean I'm supposed to just take it. 

I didn't suggest she was lying, purely that she could've been mistaken about me not being there. Why is it not obvious? I'd never even been to this surgery, and I can't go back and make another appointment, did you not read my post?

I've just switched surgeries. Also frankly I don't really give a toss if a bunch of middle aged receptionists in a shitty town think I'm a snowflake, almost anyone who's remotely competent and interesting in the professional world wouldn't do such a thing.

The receptionist was being quite rude to the elderly too though, although I feel it might be due to her being a second language english speaker and didn't have a more 'polite' vocabulary. As she was berating some old lady for not saying her date of birth loudly either.

I switched to a different surgery after and I had no problems, they were quite polite and actually managed to get me a form without first claiming that the form I spoke of didn't exist, or making me come in yesterday for no reason.

I don't really live somewhere where I'd interact with people like that, I would probably judge them and be quite annoyed. Why is it basic etiquette to know how a surgery I've never been to works, I've been to the GP a few times in my life since I've been to this country. The issue also isn't that she thinks I'm lying, its that they said I would have to go somewhere else to be seen, they didn't tell me to come back the next day and make another appointment they basically just told me they'd refuse to let me be seen. 

To be honest I'm hardly a grown man, I don't lack basic knowledge for not knowing how a system I've never used works. Funny how if I were to say a receptionist lacks basic skills, it'd somehow be me judging them and being elitist yet not knowing how her specific surgery works makes me some sort of fool.

Anyone I know who is a professional, in my career or university didn't behave this way. I don't care if a bin man thinks I'm pathetic either.

I am incredibly sharp, and intelligent that is not for debating. If I am not sharp, then you are being incredibly insulting to most people.

Why am I bitching by going on here? I don't need to avoid them, I just don't need to befriend them. I asked on here because of the issue of being refused to be seen, unfortunately you're too dense to understand just because you want to be a hard lad.

You're literally like those mechanics in Inbetweeners, that I need to randomly learn to be a 'lad' and start bantering with people, maybe I should call the receptionist 'luv' or a 'bird' too, so I can be more of a man.

I am very obviously above average intelligence, that is clear. 

It should be apparent, that I came in in the morning to book an appointment, that I would make it to the appointment. I've had retail jobs before, so its not like I am so far removed from these people that I don't know what it's like. I am hardly a mess, I have plenty of valid experience, good grades and a clear career path. I have been able to acquire experience at all the institutions I've contacted, through no parental contacts or nepotism. Obviously its great for you to argue and defend this receptionist you've never met, but you realise I've had appointments before in my life and managed to not use whatever system you've said yet I was still seen.

Why is it, if I am so prone to this, do I not have experiences like this more often? I've never had so much as a negative interaction at work.

I don't think I am above most people, I am well aware of how I stack up in intelligence to my friends and co-workers. I don't think I am even in the top half, but I do think I'm above average intelligence. I've consistently done well even when I first moved to the country, with English as a third language. If I am slow for not knowing how a surgery that I've not been to before works, then you are being incredibly rude to most people because most people don't even pick things up that they've been taught.

I find the point about school drop outs at 14 being more intelligent than people with distinctions at Masters and firsts to be bullshit, obviously its the nice oh they've got more "common sense" or they have "street sense". But its just a meaningless platitude to call that 'intelligence'.

I know plenty of people, far more intelligent than me who were doing Maths Olympiads in school and going to regional levels who were incredibly socially inept.

How did I fail to deal with the situation afterwards? I complained, they didn't listen, so I left and went to another surgery. How is that not dealt with? Did you want me to start a fight? I guess you'd love that though, be a proper man.

Imperial measures are hardly used in the world, to be honest even the small amount of imperial used here is ridiculous.

I use metric but I am aware of things like stone, feet and inches but I would never actively measure something in those formats. I'd measure in metric and if someone asked, I'd just do the conversion and tell them.

What purpose do I have to get her on side? There's other surgeries in the area and I don't actually live in the city I am currently in, I'll likely never see her again. I just went to another surgery and have an appointment for tomorrow.

Thank you for your support, I'll endeavour to become less of a fanny.

You are obviously much older than me, its the norm for most people I know to complain online about most things. 

My issue wasn't about this, my issue is that I was being refused to be seen. I am not sure how much I needed to say, basically had there not been another surgery nearby I would've had to go back to London to be seen. Surely its reasonable for me to complain about being denied an appointment. I wasn't saying that I should be seen today or at this minute, but they basically told me to go to a different surgery.

Even if I somehow made some error, I could easily be a pain and ask to see the practice manager, which my mother told me to do and write a complaint. I could take it further but honestly, I am actually trying to be seen. 

I do have quite good social skills though, or maybe my friend group are all just inept. But unless you predict some sort of societal collapse, I don't think I am particularly different from my peers and times will just change.

items.title: Why should I vote Lib over Greens?
items.text:
Why should I vote Lib over Greens?
I am fast approaching my first EU elections and I am still undecided, although the launch of CHUK has definitely put them out of the running for my vote.

I doubt I am particularly unique, I am young, based in London and very much pro-EU. I care strongly about scientific research and collaboration, with it being one of the biggest reasons I have for being a remainer.

But then I care a lot about Green issues being a Biologist and they were ahead last time in London over the Libs, I mean I am not overly fussed about the coalition as I think all the other parties have made mistakes that we all seem to brush over. In terms of economy, I am definitely not for free-market. I believe in regulation but maybe the state should have the carrot and a stick, allow private companies to progress as they please within reason and incentivise them to take certain steps (move to greener fuels for example, but then if they take advantage of public trust, more should be done to punish them.

I hear the Greens are anti-GMO right and anti-nuclear etc. which I wouldn't necessarily agree with, but then I disagree with the Lib Dem policy of wanting an entirely elected House of Lords. The hereditary lords and lords spiritual I disagree with, but I do think its good for experts to be in the Lords. Many university chancellors and top academics have a seat in the Lords and to be honest, I wish there were more there. In the political compass, I am -3.25/-3.49 but then the site says the 2017 Lib Dems are quite to the right of that and more authoritarian, so I am not really sure to trust it.

I consider myself quite political but I always find it hard to pin down, I often do the ISideWith quizzes for the UK and although my views change over the months, I tend to get Liberal Democrats first, followed by Labour and then Greens a bit behind. But then I did some EU parliament view matcher and it mostly had me with the Greens, but they asked different questions so once again difficult to reconcile. 

I guess, I want the party that is pro-institution, pro-research and not afraid to stand up to populism.

I just feel like it could be a huge benefit, lower the cost of produce, making it more resistant even possibly make it more nutritional. Obviously I feel care should be taken to prevent cross-breeding with wild relatives, but surely this can be done.

So Lib Dems are against government subsidies? So really I should be rooting for a Blairite Labour?

Institutions like universities, research institutions, museums, gardens, places where there is a public good being done in terms of research.

I don't know if I have any major ideological views, I guess I care more about society than individuals but not really in a Communist or populist sense. Like in terms of France, I'd be more on the side of Macron and increasing a carbon tax than the side of the rioters. Because I feel it's better for society in the long term. I also don't strictly see the world as some sort of class warfare being labourers and owners, I think it's more nuanced than that really.
I mean I have an ideology in that sense, but not some greater philosophical mind from history that I can put -ism after their name and live my life by.
Why would you repeat anything else? Unless you failed your exams, there's really no need to repeat basic lessons again.
Could that not just be because usually its the father who's taller, and the child gets the trait from the father?

But the father is also involved in the production of children, one set of alleles come from each parent, how would this even work?

Why does this favour the mother only and not the father?

This is just a prediction, and it uses the height of the parents and doesn't say whether or not they'll be taller than their mothers.

Using the formula provided, the child will be around 177cm, which is smaller than the mother. If the heights of the parents were switched, it'd still be the same.
No there isn't

Even if it was, we don't know to what degree intelligence is due to nature or nurture. I am from an 'uneducated' family, with nobody before me doing a degree but we come from a country without universities that was quite underdeveloped at the time.

Since the country has improved, many of my generation in the family have gone to university or are on their way to. There'd be no way to tell if my grandmother would've cut it in university or not, as there was no system in place for her to even try and go.

Now I work with many students from private schools, grammar schools, top ranked universities etc. and I don't particularly see some major difference in intelligence between us due to our backgrounds.
Yeah, although it would be nice to punish the parents for this, it will just make a bigger problem, probably how we ended up with a bunch of UKIPers.
True, I know plenty of people who despite being big on Remain, attending the marches and being part of other remain groups yet almost all will vote Labour.
I guess they think Labour is better for the rest of their policies, but really I think getting them to turn away from Labour is basically impossible.
Ironic as voting Brexit in a sense is the same as vandalising your own home.

items.title: How quickly can the hair regrow?
items.text:
How quickly can the hair regrow?
So I noticed I had a bald patch after a haircut a few weeks ago, I thought maybe it was a bad haircut but they said it was my actual hair, and they said the fact the spot was completely bald rather than having tiny hairs suggested it was alopecia areata.

I managed to see a doctor a few days later and they gave me some medicine, and I've been applying it and now I can already feel some hairs growing after a few weeks. I just wonder, was it actually alopecia areata?

One possibility that the doctor said was that, I could've had this patch for a few months under all my hair and only spotted it after my haircut and its just starting to regrow anyway. Could that be the case, false diagnosis or am I just lucky and its growing back in like a month? Although its more a few little hairs rather than thick hair like the rest of my head

Oh idk, the patch I had did look just like alopecia areata, with the ring pattern and it was like completely hairless which was what made everyone think it was alopecia, I had some blood tests although none for alopecia, just blood count, iron, glucose and thyroid but they came back normal.

Yeah, even though I've got a year of experience at a research institution which is probably a lot more useful than more taught courses in a Masters (I guess the masters project makes up for it), they still said I should do a Masters.

items.title: Staying for 4/5 days?
items.text:
Staying for 4/5 days?
Hi, I'll be staying in Cambridge in July for a few days to do a training course for a few days, although I'll be doing the course with the university I doubt I'll be really interacting with students as it seems to be aimed more towards graduates and researchers at affiliate institutions and I'll be an undergrad.

Where should I look for accommodation and is it 'lively', I mean I am not looking for wild parties but will I be able to meet some people my age (22) after the course for drinks or whatever else.

Yeah except it's part of my degree, although the majority of my course didn't do one, we all had sessions for CV writing etc, interview tips and it was heavily promoted. But not a gap year in the sense that I decided to halt my studies for this, I am also filling out a portfolio and have a bit of coursework that I am doing this year. But that will help me out as it will mean I have more free time next year with one less module to complete.

My tuition fees are waived for the year due to me doing public sector work but otherwise it'd be reduced, my living costs are covered by student finance in the same way that a regular year at uni would be.
My organisation refers to me as an intern though and I’m not really in industry, I’m in a research institution. But yeah, same thing really.

Most people don’t need to work to pay their way through uni, and it’s covered by my degree. What do you mean why should they? Because it helps and it’s amazing.

I’m literally having the best year getting to work on what I love, I’ve learned so much through this experience and networked and made new friends. How is it any different from the rest of your degree, if you can do a degree then you could do this.

It’s not the norm to be paid in my field, although some places do it but that’s more for industry jobs. But if you’re doing research at a university or public sector institution you don’t get paid. I didn’t at my institution, I know someone at a university who wasn’t paid and someone who worked for the NHS and they weren’t either
I guess not but even in my course we had some people think that if they did unpaid placements they’d have to basically foot the cost themselves
Student loan? I know very few people who needed to work to cover uni, especially as the loan is means tested
You get more if you’re in London but everywhere else is the same, and even though my uni is in Yorkshire, they adjusted my loan to do my placement in London
Yeah true but my placement was also open to graduates, we have a recent graduate doing it too although she is also unpaid.

Well I’m not lab based, but I am at probably the best institution in this field in the country/world (albeit a very niche field), I have basically got autonomy to decide how to use my data. I feel a taught masters is just more of the same, learning things for exams wasn’t crazy difficult as I am studying what I enjoy. I went from having zero prior knowledge of this area of my subject to being a lot more confident in it and being able to basically plan out my day as I want.

Which from what I’ve heard is much more akin to what a PhD in my field would be like than just doing more exams. 

Mainly the experience too, meeting big names in my field, being surrounded by this sort of community. I honestly think the ‘social’ side of seeing these people on a daily basis has done more for just in terms of confidence than anything else.

I’ve gotten to attend several conferences and talks anyway in the field I’m studying. Having people in my department basically on hand to help me with issues I have, right there in the office.

I even got to do some field work which is separate from my project but they let me go on and funded, they’ve covered my fees for a training course at another top institution for a week.
It will be July, will postgrad students still be around? I guess they’ll be busy though

My institution isn't a university so doesn't run its own PhDs and I don't want to remain in that exact subfield, its a partner for the DTP programs but they are quite competitive so I'd need a masters to stand out anyway. I mean I could probably find a PhD, as some of the previous placement students managed to jump straight to PhD.

I never said I was in industry, my institution has been doing these placement years for decades though, several of the PhD students I saw giving talks at conferences did a placement at my institution before, even some of our department heads did it in the past. I mean I'm not sure what you expect students to produce of value, but getting our work published is probably more than most undergrads have done. 

I am not sure how you could think this wasn't done, when I know several people from my course at other institutions. Almost everyone I know on placement knows other people from their course doing placements. At research institutions not industry.

As I said, I feel the experience is much more akin to PhD work than a taught masters other than the research project aspect. 

I don't know many people who managed to get paid placements in my field other than people who work at places like GSK but that's more like industry than research. It is legal and probably the norm to be unpaid, but as I said I am not in the medical/ lab based biology world and my field is pretty notorious for its lack of funding. 

Plenty of people from placement years do end up in PhDs without doing a Masters but my point is that having looked at the specific interdisciplinary program that I want to apply for, previous applicants including previous placement students have also done masters. So it's not even saying they prefer Masters to the placement, because most people had both. I mean I did see the odd person who got in straight out of undergrad, but there's probably a lot more places on offer in a BBSRC or MRC funded program than NERC ones.
